weights.why: Illustrative starting weights from the team's concept doc. Not a validated policy. Users can change them in the app.

vacant_coverage.why: A parcel counts as vacant when building footprints cover less than 2% of it (tolerates sheds and footprint edge noise).

underused_ratio.why: A parcel is flagged 'possibly underused' when its assessed improvement value is under half its land value. A common screening heuristic, not an appraisal.

capacity_acres_full.why: Capacity score is lot acres / 0.5, capped at 1. Half an acre is taken as enough for a 4-12 home project. Not a density calculation.

sb9_only_needs_availability.why: SB 9 alone allows at most 4 units (2 lots x 2 units). For a 4-12 home nonprofit project, parcels whose only pathway is SB 9 are shown only if vacant or on a surplus notice. (The 'underused' value test is too broad in Orange County, where land value dominates most older homes.)

stale_he_coverage.why: A housing-element site is flagged 'may be stale' when footprints now cover over 35% of it. Footprint vintage is unknown.

laws.about: Site tests for each land pathway. Every test cites the HCD Housing Law Fact Sheet (April 2026 versions) it was taken from. A fact sheet summary is not the statute: confirm against the Government Code before relying on any result. Tests whose data we do not have always return 'unknown'. Prototype only, not legal advice.

city_rules.about: City layer for Santa Ana. Zone descriptions come from the city's own zoning service. The category for each zone is OUR mapping of that description, not a city determination: 'review' means the zone needs a person to read the code (specific plans, specific developments, mixed zones).

data_gaps: Santa Ana's housing-element sites are not in SCAG's HousingElementSite layer (28 other OC jurisdictions are; checked 2026-11-07). Housing-element flags are therefore empty for Santa Ana.
Owner type (needed for SB 4) is not in free parcel data. Places of worship from OpenStreetMap are used as a lead, not a fact.
No historic-district, wetlands, farmland or earthquake-fault layer is loaded. Those tests show 'unknown'.
Tenancy history (SB 9, SB 684) is not public and would be personal information. Always 'unknown'.
Fire hazard zones come from the OC county LRA copy and CAL FIRE's statewide SRA layer. CAL FIRE's 2025 LRA maps were not loaded.
